newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, Eurodollars flat ahead Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, Eurodollars flat ahead Fed meeting.

text.p: Japanese and U.S. interest rate futures traded on SIMEX were trapped in tight ranges on Monday as most participants retreated to the sidelines ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting.

Dealers said there was no clear consensus on whether the Fed would move to raise rates again in view of a mixed bag of U.S. economic data and Fed chief Alan Greenspan's recent comments that he expected growth to slow later this year.
"Three weeks ago, there was an 80:20 chance of a raise. Now it's about 50:50. I don't think they will do anything until maybe July," a trader with a U.S. futures house said.

He said there had been large spread trades on Eurodollar futures in Chicago on Friday, with players buying June and selling September, reflecting the expectation that rates would be hiked only after June.
June Eurodollars ended at 94.095 against their IMM close at 94.100 on volume of 4,920 lots. September ended at 93.890 against 93.895.
The dealer said the market showed more of a downside risk as players had largely priced in steady rates, while a rate hike by the Fed could prompt a sell-off.

Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures were unlikely to be dampened by a U.S. rate hike as the yen's recent steep rise against the dollar had reduced expectations of higher rates in Japan for the time being, dealers said.
The lead December Euroyen contract stood at 98.98 at 1115 GMT after hitting an early high of 98.99 against its IMM close at 98.97.
Dealers said the contract faced heavy selling pressure around the 99.00 level.
"The whole world is selling at 99.00. But after the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting, we should trade higher to 99.06/08," the trader said.
June JGBs ended at 124.48 against their previous 124.21.
